verses.text: A Psalm of David. I call upon You, O LORD; come quickly to me. Hear my voice when I call to You.

xrefs.text: But I am poor and needy; hurry to me, O God. You are my help and my deliverer; O LORD, do not delay.
Be pleased, O LORD, to deliver me; hurry, O LORD, to help me.
Be not far from me, O God. Hurry, O my God, to help me.
Hide not Your face from Your servant, for I am in distress. Answer me quickly!
Answer me quickly, O LORD; my spirit fails. Do not hide Your face from me, or I will be like those who descend to the Pit.

verses.text: May my prayer be set before You like incense; my uplifted hands, like the evening offering.

xrefs.text: Then another angel, who had a golden censer, came and stood at the altar. He was given much incense to offer, along with the prayers of all the saints, on the golden altar before the throne.

When He had taken the scroll, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb. Each one had a harp, and they were holding golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.
Therefore I want the men everywhere to pray, lifting up holy hands, without anger or dissension.

For My name will be great among the nations, from where the sun rises to where it sets. In every place, incense and pure offerings will be presented in My name, because My name will be great among the nations,” says the LORD of Hosts.
while I was still praying, Gabriel, the man I had seen in the earlier vision, came to me in swift flight about the time of the evening sacrifice.

verses.text: Set a guard, O LORD, over my mouth; keep watch at the door of my lips.

xrefs.text: If anyone considers himself religious and yet does not bridle his tongue, he deceives his heart and his religion is worthless.
For the choirmaster. For Jeduthun. A Psalm of David. I said, “I will watch my ways so that I will not sin with my tongue; I will guard my mouth with a muzzle as long as the wicked are present.”
Do not rely on a friend; do not trust in a companion. Seal the doors of your mouth from her who lies in your arms.
Keep your tongue from evil and your lips from deceitful speech.
We all stumble in many ways. If anyone is never at fault in what he says, he is a perfect man, able to control his whole body.

verses.text: Do not let my heart be drawn to any evil thing or take part in works of wickedness with men who do iniquity; let me not feast on their delicacies.

xrefs.text: Turn my heart to Your testimonies and not to covetous gain.
And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.
Do not be deceived: “Bad company corrupts good character.”
Why, O LORD, do You make us stray from Your ways and harden our hearts from fearing You? Return, for the sake of Your servants, the tribes of Your heritage.
“Therefore come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord. Touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you.”

verses.text: Let the righteous man strike me; let his rebuke be an act of loving devotion. It is oil for my head; let me not refuse it. For my prayer is ever against the deeds of the wicked.

xrefs.text: It is better to heed a wise man’s rebuke than to listen to the song of fools.
Those I love I rebuke and discipline. Therefore be earnest and repent.
Brothers, if someone is caught in a trespass, you who are spiritual should restore him with a spirit of gentleness. But watch yourself, or you also may be tempted.
Better an open rebuke than love that is concealed.
Like an earring of gold or an ornament of fine gold is a wise man’s rebuke to a listening ear.

verses.text: When their rulers are thrown down from the cliffs, the people will listen to my words, for they are pleasant.

xrefs.text: and the army of Judah also captured 10,000 men alive. They took them to the top of a cliff and threw them down so that all were dashed to pieces.
Now the Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before them, and many fell slain on Mount Gilboa.
Then all Israel came together to David at Hebron and said, “Here we are, your own flesh and blood.
These are the last words of David: “The oracle of David son of Jesse, the oracle of the man raised on high, the one anointed by the God of Jacob, and the sweet psalmist of Israel:
Now the Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before them, and many fell slain on Mount Gilboa.

verses.text: As when one plows and breaks up the soil, so our bones have been scattered at the mouth of Sheol.

xrefs.text: As it is written: “For Your sake we face death all day long; we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered.”
There they are, overwhelmed with dread, where there was nothing to fear. For God has scattered the bones of those who besieged you. You put them to shame, for God has despised them.
Yet for Your sake we face death all day long; we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered.
Their bodies will lie in the street of the great city— figuratively called Sodom and Egypt— where their Lord was also crucified.
So the king ordered Doeg, “You turn and strike down the priests!” And Doeg the Edomite turned and struck down the priests himself. On that day he killed eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod.

verses.text: But my eyes are fixed on You, O GOD the Lord. In You I seek refuge; do not leave my soul defenseless.

xrefs.text: A song of ascents. I lift up my eyes to You, the One enthroned in heaven.
Our God, will You not judge them? For we are powerless before this vast army that comes against us. We do not know what to do, but our eyes are upon You.”
The poor and needy seek water, but there is none; their tongues are parched with thirst. I, the LORD, will answer them; I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.
He will turn toward the prayer of the destitute; He will not despise their prayer.
My eyes are always on the LORD, for He will free my feet from the mesh.

verses.text: Keep me from the snares they have laid for me, and from the lures of evildoers.

xrefs.text: So they watched Him closely and sent spies who pretended to be sincere. They were hoping to catch Him in His words in order to hand Him over to the rule and authority of the governor.
The wicked have set a snare for me, but I have not strayed from Your precepts.
The proud hide a snare for me; the cords of their net are spread along the path, and lures are set out for me. Selah
The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life, turning one from the snares of death.
Those who seek my life lay snares; those who wish me harm speak destruction, plotting deceit all day long.

verses.text: Let the wicked fall into their own nets, while I pass by in safety.

xrefs.text: May ruin befall them by surprise; may the net they hid ensnare them; may they fall into the hazard they created.
May the heads of those who surround me be covered in the trouble their lips have caused.
But God will shoot them with arrows; suddenly they will be wounded.
So they hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai. Then the fury of the king subsided.
The righteous man is delivered from trouble; in his place the wicked man goes in.
